```{r load}
library(wet)
library(ggplot2)
sf::sf_use_s2(FALSE)

vd <- function(f) system.file("vignette-data", f, package = "wet")
daily <- readRDS(vd("station_daily.rds"))
prov <- attr(daily, "provenance")
map <- readRDS(vd("station_map.rds"))
lh <- utils::read.csv(vd("life_history_bulk.csv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE, na.strings = "")

to_title <- function(x) {
  vapply(strsplit(tolower(x), " "), function(w) {
    big <- !w %in% c("at", "the", "near", "of")
    w[big] <- paste0(toupper(substring(w[big], 1, 1)), substring(w[big], 2))
    paste(w, collapse = " ")
  }, "")
}
station_label <- stats::setNames(
  sprintf("%s (%s)", to_title(prov$stations$station_name), prov$stations$station_number),
  prov$stations$station_number
)
stations <- names(station_label)
short_name <- function(st) sub(" \\(.*", "", station_label[[st]])

# chinook timing windows that stay in open water: a window touching November-April
# rests on flows read under ice, so it is left out rather than corrected
ice_months <- c(11:12, 1:4)
touches_ice <- function(start, end) {
  a <- as.Date(paste0("2001-", start))
  b <- as.Date(paste0(2001 + (end < start), "-", sub("02-29", "02-28", end)))
  any(as.integer(format(seq(a, b, by = "day"), "%m")) %in% ice_months)
}
ch <- lh[lh$species_code == "CH", ]
open_water <- !mapply(touches_ice, ch$start, ch$end)
stopifnot(identical(ch$life_stage[open_water], c("migration", "spawning", "fry_migration")))
out <- ch[!open_water, ]
ch <- ch[open_water, ]
# fry migration lies inside migration and spawning together (checked below), so it is not shown
fry <- ch[ch$life_stage == "fry_migration", ]
ch <- ch[ch$life_stage != "fry_migration", ]
stage <- sub("_", " ", ch$life_stage)
windows <- data.frame(window = paste0(toupper(substring(stage, 1, 1)), substring(stage, 2)),
                      start = ch$start, end = ch$end)
md_text <- function(md) {
  d <- as.Date(paste0("2001-", md))
  paste(format(d, "%B"), as.integer(format(d, "%d")))
}
md_short <- function(md) {
  d <- as.Date(paste0("2001-", md))
  paste(format(d, "%b"), as.integer(format(d, "%d")))
}
window_label <- stats::setNames(sprintf("%s\n%s – %s", windows$window, md_short(windows$start),
                                        md_short(windows$end)), windows$window)
span_text <- function(w) {
  k <- which(windows$window == w)
  paste(md_text(windows$start[k]), "to", md_text(windows$end[k]))
}
days_of <- function(k) {
  seq(as.Date(paste0("2001-", windows$start[k])), as.Date(paste0("2001-", windows$end[k])), by = "day")
}
win_days <- stats::setNames(vapply(seq_len(nrow(windows)), function(k) length(days_of(k)), 0L),
                            windows$window)
# a window-year counts when this share of its days has flow (wet_window_stats())
need_text <- paste0(round(100 * formals(wet_window_stats)$min_frac), "%")
left_out <- sub("_", " ", out$life_stage)
# the recipe chunk below types these dates; fail here if the table moves under it
stopifnot(identical(windows$start, c("05-01", "08-01")), identical(windows$end, c("08-01", "09-15")))
# "its fry migration window falls within these two": every fry day is a migration or spawning day
fry_days <- seq(as.Date(paste0("2001-", fry$start)), as.Date(paste0("2001-", fry$end)), by = "day")
stopifnot(nrow(fry) == 1, all(fry_days %in% do.call(c, lapply(seq_len(nrow(windows)), days_of))))
# the limits name one source for both windows, neither carried over from another watershed's row
stopifnot(identical(unique(ch$source), "gottesfeld_rabnett2007SkeenaFish"), !any(grepl("other area", ch$note)))

baseline <- 1981:2010
# the title names this period; fail if the article moves to another
stopifnot(identical(baseline, 1981:2010))
min_baseline <- 10
base_text <- paste0(min(baseline), "–", max(baseline))
# the last ten years, the decade the sibling article ends on too
recent <- 2016:2025
last_year <- max(recent)
recent_text <- paste0(min(recent), "–", max(recent))
# every window must be over in the last year, or its last bar is a part-year
stopifnot(all(as.Date(paste0(last_year, "-", windows$end)) <= max(daily$date)))

# colours come from the gq registries, so no hex literal appears in this
# vignette; assert each class set, because a malformed CSV row adds a layer silently
reg <- gq::gq_reg_custom(system.file("cartography", "wet_station.csv", package = "wet"))
reg_main <- gq::gq_reg_main()
classes <- function(layer, expect) {
  x <- gq::gq_tmap_classes(reg$layers[[layer]])
  stopifnot(identical(names(x$values), expect))
  list(values = x$values, labels = stats::setNames(x$labels, names(x$values)))
}
pal_hydro <- classes("hydrograph", c("band", "median", "window"))
pal_hydro$labels <- sub("^Baseline", base_text, pal_hydro$labels)
pal_side <- classes("recent_departure", c("below", "above"))
pal_map <- classes("station_map", c("catchment_main", "catchment_buck", "stream_main", "station"))
# labels that restate a variable are built from it, not read from the registry
pal_side$labels[] <- paste(c("Below", "Above"), "the", base_text, "mean")

theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
            theme(legend.position = "bottom", panel.grid.minor = element_blank()))
pct <- function(x) paste0(round(abs(x)), "%")
day_text <- function(d) paste(as.integer(format(d, "%d")), format(d, "%B %Y"))
by_station <- function(d) {
  d$station_number <- factor(d$station_number, stations)
  d
}
by_window <- function(d, rev = FALSE) {
  lv <- if (rev) rev(windows$window) else windows$window
  d$period <- factor(d$period, lv)
  d
}
years_text <- function(y) {
  y <- sort(unique(y))
  runs <- split(y, cumsum(c(1, diff(y) != 1)))
  one <- function(r) if (length(r) > 1) paste0(r[1], "–", r[length(r)]) else as.character(r)
  sub(", ([^,]*)$", " and \\1", paste(vapply(runs, one, ""), collapse = ", "))
}
and_text <- function(x) sub(", ([^,]*)$", " and \\1", paste(x, collapse = ", "))
```

```{r stats}
stats <- wet_window_stats(daily, windows, stats = "mean")

# baseline years per station and window; every one must clear min_baseline,
# because nothing below says what happens to a window that does not
qb <- stats[stats$variable == "q_mean" & stats$year %in% baseline, ]
nb <- merge(expand.grid(station_number = stations, period = windows$window,
                        stringsAsFactors = FALSE),
            stats::aggregate(year ~ station_number + period, qb, length), all.x = TRUE)
nb$year[is.na(nb$year)] <- 0L
stopifnot(all(nb$year >= min_baseline))
# 08EE003's baseline years, the same in every window (the prose states them once)
y003 <- split(qb$year[qb$station_number == "08EE003"], qb$period[qb$station_number == "08EE003"])
stopifnot(length(unique(lapply(y003, sort))) == 1)
base_003 <- years_text(y003[[1]])
miss_003 <- setdiff(baseline, y003[[1]])
# the opening, the caption and the limits say 08EE003's baseline is shorter than the period
stopifnot(length(miss_003) > 0)
# baseline years missing at every station and window, for the limits bullet
miss_text <- vapply(stations, function(st) {
  m <- vapply(windows$window, function(w) {
    paste(setdiff(baseline, qb$year[qb$station_number == st & qb$period == w]), collapse = " ")
  }, "")
  m <- m[nzchar(m)]
  if (!length(m)) return(NA_character_)
  parts <- vapply(unique(m), function(k) {
    w <- names(m)[m == k]
    where <- if (length(w) == nrow(windows)) "every window" else tolower(and_text(w))
    sprintf("%s in %s", years_text(as.integer(strsplit(k, " ")[[1]])), where)
  }, "")
  sprintf("%s lacks %s", short_name(st), paste(parts, collapse = ", and "))
}, "")
miss_text <- paste(miss_text[!is.na(miss_text)], collapse = "; ")

# baseline and departure from cd, one station per call
cols_flag <- c("variable", "period", "year", "value", "n_days", "frac_provisional")
dep <- lapply(stations, function(st) {
  x <- stats[stats$station_number == st, ]
  x$station_number <- NULL
  # cd warns of baseline years with no data; base_003 states them instead
  b <- suppressWarnings(cd::cd_baseline(x, baseline))
  a <- merge(cd::cd_anomaly(x, b), x[cols_flag], by = c("variable", "period", "year"))
  list(baseline = cbind(station_number = st, b),
       anomaly = cbind(station_number = st, a))
})
pick <- function(k) do.call(rbind, lapply(dep, `[[`, k))
base <- pick("baseline")
anom <- pick("anomaly")
```

```{r recent-data}
kf <- anom[anom$variable == "q_mean" & anom$year %in% recent, ]
stopifnot(!anyNA(kf$anomaly))
# the recent years each gauge lacks: Buck Creek has no 2016 in either window, and nothing else is missing
miss_recent <- lapply(stats::setNames(stations, stations), function(st) {
  setdiff(recent, kf$year[kf$station_number == st])
})
stopifnot(identical(miss_recent[["08EE013"]], 2016L), length(miss_recent[["08EE003"]]) == 0,
          nrow(kf) == (length(recent) * length(stations) - 1) * nrow(windows))
n_recent <- vapply(miss_recent, function(m) length(recent) - length(m), 0L)
kf$pct <- 100 + kf$anomaly
kf$side <- ifelse(kf$pct < 100, "below", "above")
kf$status <- ifelse(kf$frac_provisional > 0, "provisional", "approved")

# the median baseline year, as % of cd's baseline mean: in a skewed record a
# typical year sits under the mean, and the figure has to show that
bq <- base[base$variable == "q_mean", ]
ref <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(bq)), function(i) {
  v <- qb$value[qb$station_number == bq$station_number[i] & qb$period == bq$period[i]]
  stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(mean(v), bq$baseline_mean[i])))
  data.frame(station_number = bq$station_number[i], period = bq$period[i],
             mean_q = bq$baseline_mean[i], median_pct = 100 * stats::median(v) / mean(v),
             q10 = stats::quantile(v, 0.1, names = FALSE), q_min = min(v))
}))
ref$label <- sprintf("Mean %s m³/s", vapply(signif(ref$mean_q, 2), format, "", drop0trailing = TRUE))

# the claims below, each computed from kf and ref
kr <- merge(kf, ref, by = c("station_number", "period"))
low_years <- recent[vapply(recent, function(y) all(kr$pct[kr$year == y] < 100), TRUE)]
stopifnot(length(low_years) >= 2)
# "From <first low year>, every bar falls below ...": the low years run unbroken to the last year
stopifnot(identical(low_years, min(low_years):last_year))
# "below normal in every timing window at both gauges in <low_years>": every window
# and station is in kr for each of those years
stopifnot(all(table(kr$year[kr$year %in% low_years]) == nrow(windows) * length(stations)))
low <- kr[kr$year %in% low_years, ]
# value is the window mean itself, carried from wet_window_stats() into anom
stopifnot(is.numeric(low[["value"]]), !anyNA(low[["value"]]))
n_low <- nrow(low)
n_dec <- sum(low$value < low$q10)
# "drier than nine baseline years in ten", read as the share of that window's baseline years
# wetter than the bar; the quantile count must agree with it (08EE003 has only 18 years)
share_wetter <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(low)), function(i) {
  v <- qb$value[qb$station_number == low$station_number[i] & qb$period == low$period[i]]
  mean(v > low$value[i])
}, 0)
stopifnot(n_dec == sum(share_wetter >= 0.9))
# the opening says "N of those were drier than nine years in ten": at least one
stopifnot(n_dec > 0)
n_min <- sum(low$value < low$q_min)
stopifnot(n_min > 0)   # "and N were drier than any 1981-2010 year"
# "every bar from those years falls below the median year as well as the mean"
stopifnot(all(low$pct < low$median_pct))
# "before <first low year> the decade swings both ways": in every window at both gauges, some
# earlier year sits above normal and some below
early <- kr[kr$year < min(low_years), ]
swing <- stats::aggregate(pct ~ station_number + period, early, function(p) any(p >= 100) && any(p < 100))
stopifnot(nrow(swing) == nrow(windows) * length(stations), all(swing$pct))
# "the two gauges fall on the same side of normal in all but N of the M window-years both recorded"
both <- stats::aggregate(side ~ period + year, kr, function(s) if (length(s) == 2) length(unique(s)) == 1 else NA)
both <- both[!is.na(both$side), ]
n_both <- nrow(both)
n_split <- sum(!both$side)
stopifnot(n_split == 1)   # the prose says "all but one"
med_range <- range(ref$median_pct)
# "a typical year sits under the mean": every median below it, as printed
stopifnot(round(med_range[2]) < 100)
# bars resting on fewer than all of their window's days
part <- kf[kf$n_days < win_days[kf$period], ]
stopifnot(nrow(part) > 0)   # the limits bullet says some bars have days missing
part_text <- paste(vapply(split(part, paste(part$station_number, part$year)), function(d) {
  sprintf("%s in %d (%s)", short_name(d$station_number[1]), d$year[1],
          tolower(and_text(intersect(windows$window, d$period))))
}, ""), collapse = "; ")
part_share <- range(100 * part$n_days / win_days[part$period])

cap_recent <- sprintf(paste(
  "Mean flow in each chinook salmon life history timing window, %s, as a percentage of its %s mean (solid line, given",
  "in m³/s at the top right of each panel). Each bar is labelled with its percentage, coloured by",
  "whether it falls below or above the mean, and paler where any of its days are provisional. The",
  "dashed line is the median %s year. At %s, the %s normal rests on %s: no window in %s has %s",
  "of its days."
), recent_text, base_text, base_text, station_label[["08EE003"]], base_text, base_003,
years_text(miss_003), need_text)
```

```{r change-data}
# change in each window's mean flow, from its 1981-2010 mean to the mean of 2016-2025, with the
# middle 90% of changes from resampling the years of each period (with replacement). At these years it
# covers 83-87% of no-change records, under the 87% bar (data/checks/departure_interval_coverage.txt),
# so it is not called a 90% range and no count rests on it. That report measured this bundle: a rebuilt
# one needs the script rerun before this sentence stands
stopifnot(identical(unname(tools::md5sum(vd("station_daily.rds"))), "2ab0f5833ebbac35161c593ac248b7a3"))
set.seed(145)
n_draw <- 5000
chg <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(ref)), function(i) {
  st <- ref$station_number[i]
  w <- ref$period[i]
  b <- qb$value[qb$station_number == st & qb$period == w]
  r <- kf$value[kf$station_number == st & kf$period == w]
  stopifnot(length(r) == n_recent[[st]], isTRUE(all.equal(mean(b), ref$mean_q[i])))
  draws <- replicate(n_draw, mean(sample(r, replace = TRUE)) / mean(sample(b, replace = TRUE)))
  q <- stats::quantile(100 * (draws - 1), c(0.05, 0.95), names = FALSE)
  data.frame(station_number = st, period = w, pct = 100 * (mean(r) / mean(b) - 1), lo = q[1], hi = q[2])
}))
stopifnot(nrow(chg) == nrow(windows) * length(stations))
# "below its normal in every timing window at both gauges, by <min>-<max>"
stopifnot(all(chg$pct < 0))
chg_range <- range(abs(chg$pct))
cap_change <- sprintf(paste(
  "Change in each chinook salmon life history timing window's mean flow, from its %s mean to the mean of %s, at each",
  "gauge (point); the bar spans the middle 90%% of changes from resampling the years in each period,",
  "and the vertical line is no change."
), base_text, recent_text)
```

The R package [`wet`](https://newgraphenvironment.github.io/wet/) [@wet] measures stream flow and
water temperature on British Columbia's Freshwater Atlas. This case study measures summer flow at two
long-record gauges near Houston, in the weeks when chinook salmon migrate and spawn, against its
`r base_text` normal. That period is one of the World Meteorological Organization's 30-year standard
normals [@arguez_vose2011DefinitionStandard, p. 699; @worldmeteorologicalorganization2017WMOGuidelines],
and the one `wet`'s published flows are normals of: its water balance runs on
[`climr`](https://bcgov.github.io/climr/)'s `r base_text` climate [@climr], and its routed flow is the
`r base_text` mean of the Pacific Climate Impacts Consortium's model run
[@schnorbus2018VICGlacierVICGL; @craig_etal2020Flexiblewatershed; @werner_etal2019longtermtemporally].
It already holds part of recent warming [@hansen_etal2012Perceptionclimate], so
[Rebuilding Stream Flow History Where Gauges Are Few](flow-change-sparse-gauges.html) measures change
from 1951–1980 instead.

**The answer.** Over `r recent_text`, mean flow in every chinook salmon life history timing window at both gauges was below
its `r base_text` normal, by `r pct(chg_range[1])` to `r pct(chg_range[2])`. Every window at both gauges was below normal in
each year from `r min(low_years)`, and `r n_dec` of those `r n_low` window means were drier than nine
`r base_text` years in ten. At `r short_name("08EE003")`, the normal rests on `r base_003`, the years
with enough record.

## Where are the gauges?

```{r map-data}
catch <- map$catchments
catch$part <- ifelse(catch$station_number == "08EE013", "catchment_buck", "catchment_main")
catch <- catch[order(catch$part != "catchment_main"), ]   # the larger one first, beneath
buck_share <- with(sf::st_drop_geometry(catch),
                   area_km2[station_number == "08EE013"] / area_km2[station_number == "08EE003"])
# the map claims Buck Creek's catchment lies inside the Bulkley gauge's
inside <- sf::st_area(sf::st_intersection(sf::st_geometry(catch[catch$part == "catchment_buck", ]),
                                          sf::st_geometry(catch[catch$part == "catchment_main", ])))
stopifnot(as.numeric(inside) / as.numeric(sf::st_area(catch[catch$part == "catchment_buck", ])) > 0.99)
# "both gauges are near Houston", measured from each gauge
d_town <- stats::setNames(as.numeric(sf::st_distance(map$stations, map$places)), map$stations$station_number)
stopifnot(all(d_town < 10000))
# each stream placed from its mouth: the river it joins (its watershed code) and the town by it
mouth_of <- function(s) map$mouths[map$mouths$stream == s, ]
town_of <- function(name) map$towns[map$towns$name == name, ]
km_between <- function(a, b) as.numeric(sf::st_distance(a, b)) / 1000
into_buck <- mouth_of("buck")$into1
into_bulkley <- mouth_of("bulkley")$into1
stopifnot(identical(into_buck, "Bulkley River"), identical(into_bulkley, "Skeena River"),
          km_between(mouth_of("buck"), town_of("Houston")) < 2,       # "joins ... in the town"
          km_between(mouth_of("bulkley"), town_of("Hazelton")) < 2)   # "joins ... at Hazelton"
# Hazelton from Houston: the distance and compass point the sentence gives
hz <- sf::st_coordinates(town_of("Hazelton")) - sf::st_coordinates(town_of("Houston"))
hz_km <- round(sqrt(sum(hz^2)) / 1000, -1)
hz_deg <- (atan2(hz[1], hz[2]) * 180 / pi) %% 360
hz_dir <- c("north", "north-east", "east", "south-east", "south", "south-west", "west",
            "north-west")[(round(hz_deg / 45) %% 8) + 1]
# the caption: drawn streams are order 5 and up, plus the two gauged streams whole; lakes 100 ha and up
stopifnot(all(map$streams$stream_order >= 5 | map$streams$main), all(map$lakes$area_ha >= 100))
# data-raw/station_vignette_map.R selects the thin streams and the lakes in a box 8 km beyond the
# catchments, but a lake comes back whole; the caption says they are drawn only near the catchments,
# so both are cut to that box here
near <- sf::st_as_sfc(sf::st_bbox(sf::st_buffer(sf::st_union(map$catchments), 8000)))
cut_near <- function(x) {
  x <- suppressWarnings(sf::st_intersection(x, near))
  x[!sf::st_is_empty(x), ]
}
thin_streams <- cut_near(map$streams[!map$streams$main, ])
lakes_near <- cut_near(map$lakes)
# the caption names both layers: each must survive the cut, as lines and polygons (a feature
# touching the box edge would come back a point, a mark the caption does not name)
stopifnot(nrow(thin_streams) > 0, nrow(lakes_near) > 0,
          all(sf::st_geometry_type(thin_streams) %in% c("LINESTRING", "MULTILINESTRING")),
          all(sf::st_geometry_type(lakes_near) %in% c("POLYGON", "MULTIPOLYGON")))

map_w <- 7
map_h <- 6.5
bb <- sf::st_bbox(sf::st_buffer(sf::st_union(catch), 3000))
# room below the catchments for the legend and scale bar, so neither covers them
bb[["ymin"]] <- bb[["ymin"]] - 0.22 * (bb[["ymax"]] - bb[["ymin"]])
bb <- gq::gq_bbox_aspect(bb, asp = map_w / map_h)
lim_x <- c(bb[["xmin"]], bb[["xmax"]])
lim_y <- c(bb[["ymin"]], bb[["ymax"]])
dx <- diff(lim_x)
dy <- diff(lim_y)

st <- map$stations
xy <- sf::st_coordinates(st)
# 08EE003 sits just west of Buck Creek's mouth and near the frame's west edge:
# its label goes above and right, Buck Creek's to the right, Houston's below left
west <- xy[, 1] == min(xy[, 1])
st_lab <- data.frame(x = xy[, 1] + ifelse(west, -0.01, 0.015) * dx,
                     y = xy[, 2] + ifelse(west, 0.03, 0) * dy,
                     label = station_label[st$station_number], vjust = ifelse(west, 0, 0.5))
pl <- sf::st_coordinates(map$places)
# the town point sits under Buck Creek's marker, so the town is a label below it
pl_lab <- data.frame(x = pl[, 1], y = pl[, 2] - 0.035 * dy, label = map$places$name)

stream_sty <- reg_main$layers$streams_all$classification$classes$WA24111110
lake_sty <- reg_main$layers$lake
town_sty <- reg_main$layers$town
main_streams <- map$streams[map$streams$main, ]

# scale bar in the lower right, its length from gq
sb_km <- max(gq::gq_scale_breaks(bb))
sb <- data.frame(x = lim_x[2] - 0.05 * dx - sb_km * 1000, y = lim_y[1] + 0.05 * dy)
sb$xend <- sb$x + sb_km * 1000

# keymap: BC with the map extent, in the upper right
key <- ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = map$bc, fill = "white", colour = pal_hydro$values[["median"]], linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_sf(data = sf::st_as_sfc(bb), fill = NA, colour = pal_map$values[["station"]], linewidth = 0.6) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = pal_hydro$values[["median"]],
                                        linewidth = 0.3))
key_w <- 0.24 * dx
key_h <- key_w * 1.05

cap_map <- sprintf(paste(
  "The two gauges (points) and the land each one drains (shaded). Buck Creek's catchment (%s km²)",
  "lies inside the Bulkley gauge's (%s km²), so the two records are not independent. The Bulkley",
  "River and Buck Creek are drawn heavy; other streams of order 5 and up (thin) and lakes of 100 ha",
  "and up (blue) are drawn only near the catchments. Houston is labelled, the bar is %s km, and the",
  "inset places the map in British Columbia."
), format(round(catch$area_km2[catch$part == "catchment_buck"]), big.mark = ","),
format(round(catch$area_km2[catch$part == "catchment_main"]), big.mark = ","), sb_km)
```

Both gauges are near Houston. Buck Creek joins the `r into_buck` in the town, and the Bulkley gauge
sits downstream of its mouth, so it measures Buck Creek's flow as well: Buck Creek drains
`r pct(100 * buck_share)` of the area above it. The Bulkley joins the `r into_bulkley` at Hazelton,
about `r hz_km` km `r hz_dir` of Houston.

## What is a chinook salmon life history timing window?

A chinook salmon life history timing window, or window for short, is a stretch of the year when chinook use a stream for one thing.
In the upper Bulkley River, the early run of chinook passes Moricetown Canyon before about July 30, and
chinook spawn in August and September [@gottesfeld_rabnett2007SkeenaFish, p. 355]. New Graph's
species-timing table sets the Bulkley's windows from that report: adult migration from
`r span_text("Migration")`, and spawning from `r span_text("Spawning")`. Its fry migration window falls
within these two, so it is not shown on its own, and its other `r nrow(out)` chinook windows,
`r and_text(left_out)`, reach into November–April, when the gauges can read under ice, so they are left
out. A window's flow in a year is its mean daily flow, counted when `r need_text` of its days have a record.

## How did the last ten years compare with normal?

Each bar is one chinook salmon life history timing window in one year: its mean flow as a percentage of that window's
`r base_text` mean, so 100% is normal and lower is drier. Wet years pull the mean up, so a typical year
sits under it; the dashed line marks the median year.

Before `r min(low_years)` the decade swings both ways in every window. From `r min(low_years)`,
every bar falls below the median year as well as the mean, and `r n_min` were drier than any
`r base_text` year. The two gauges fall on the same side of normal in
all but one of the `r n_both` window-years both recorded, partly because one catchment holds the
other.

```{r recent, fig.height = 5, fig.cap = cap_recent}
kf <- by_window(by_station(kf))
ref <- by_window(by_station(ref))
ymax <- max(kf$pct) * 1.2
refs <- rbind(data.frame(ref[c("station_number", "period")], y = 100, line = "mean"),
              data.frame(ref[c("station_number", "period")], y = ref$median_pct, line = "median"))
ggplot(kf, aes(year, pct)) +
  geom_col(aes(fill = side, alpha = status), width = 0.75) +
  geom_hline(data = refs, aes(yintercept = y, linetype = line), colour = pal_hydro$values[["median"]],
             linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_text(aes(label = pct(pct)), vjust = -0.35, size = 2.7) +
  # the mean in m3/s, top right, clear of the first year's bars
  geom_text(data = ref, aes(x = max(recent) + 0.45, y = ymax, label = label), hjust = 1,
            vjust = 1, size = 2.7, colour = pal_hydro$values[["median"]]) +
  facet_grid(station_number ~ period, labeller = labeller(
    station_number = as_labeller(sub(" \\(", "\n(", station_label)),
    period = as_labeller(window_label))) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pal_side$values, labels = pal_side$labels, name = NULL) +
  scale_alpha_manual(values = c(approved = 1, provisional = 0.45),
                     labels = c(approved = "Approved", provisional = "Provisional"), name = NULL) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c(mean = "solid", median = "22"),
                        labels = c(mean = paste(base_text, "mean"),
                                   median = paste("Median", base_text, "year")), name = NULL) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%"), limits = c(0, ymax),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0))) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = recent) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = paste("Percent of", base_text, "mean")) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(order = 1), alpha = guide_legend(
    order = 2, override.aes = list(fill = pal_side$values[["below"]])),
    linetype = guide_legend(order = 3, override.aes = list(linewidth = 0.5))) +
  theme(panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(), strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0),
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        legend.box = "vertical", legend.spacing.y = unit(0, "pt"), legend.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0))
```

## What did the year look like?

```{r hydro-data}
doy_of <- function(date) {
  j <- as.integer(format(date, "%j"))
  y <- as.integer(format(date, "%Y"))
  leap <- (y %% 4 == 0 & y %% 100 != 0) | y %% 400 == 0
  ifelse(leap & j > 59, j - 1L, j)
}
h <- daily[format(daily$date, "%m-%d") != "02-29", ]
h$doy <- doy_of(h$date)
h$year <- as.integer(format(h$date, "%Y"))
# the mean and median day of each period, on days with at least `need` years of record;
# every day of the year is kept, so a day without enough years breaks the line. The 1981-2010
# line uses only the years each gauge's window normals use (qb: 1981-1998 at the Bulkley gauge),
# so it is the normal the rest of the article describes
# a recent line counts a day only where every one of that gauge's recent years has it
day_stats <- function(d, period, need) {
  out <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(d, list(d$station_number, d$doy), drop = TRUE), function(x) {
    data.frame(station_number = x$station_number[1], doy = x$doy[1], n = nrow(x),
               mean = mean(x$q_m3s), median = stats::median(x$q_m3s))
  }))
  nd <- if (length(need) == 1) need else need[out$station_number]
  out[out$n < nd, c("mean", "median")] <- NA
  grid <- expand.grid(station_number = stations, doy = 1:365, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  out <- merge(grid, out, all.x = TRUE)
  rbind(data.frame(out[c("station_number", "doy")], period = period, stat = "mean", q = out$mean),
        data.frame(out[c("station_number", "doy")], period = period, stat = "median", q = out$median))
}
norm_years <- split(qb$year, qb$station_number)
in_norm <- paste(h$station_number, h$year) %in% paste(qb$station_number, qb$year)
yr <- rbind(day_stats(h[in_norm, ], "base", min_baseline),
            day_stats(h[h$year %in% recent, ], "recent", n_recent))
# each line averages only its period's years: the normal's, and every recent one the gauge has
stopifnot(all(h$year[in_norm] %in% baseline),
          identical(sort(unique(h$year[in_norm & h$station_number == "08EE003"])), sort(unique(norm_years[["08EE003"]]))))
yr <- yr[order(yr$station_number, yr$period, yr$stat, yr$doy), ]
yr$date <- as.Date("2001-01-01") + yr$doy - 1
# both gauges' normal lines cover every timing window; the recent lines break where a year has no record
in_win <- yr$doy >= doy_of(as.Date("2001-05-01")) & yr$doy <= doy_of(as.Date("2001-09-15"))
stopifnot(!anyNA(yr$q[in_win & yr$period == "base"]),
          all(tapply(!is.na(yr$q[yr$period == "recent"]), yr$station_number[yr$period == "recent"], any)))
# the dates the Bulkley gauge's normal covers, for the caption: one unbroken stretch
b003 <- yr[yr$station_number == "08EE003" & yr$period == "base" & yr$stat == "mean" & !is.na(yr$q), ]
stopifnot(all(diff(b003$doy) == 1))
span_003 <- paste(day_text(min(b003$date)), "to", day_text(max(b003$date)))
span_003 <- gsub(" 2001", "", span_003)

# two panels per gauge: the whole year with the migration window beneath, and July to October with
# the spawning window, on its own scale so the low summer flow is not dwarfed by the freshet
zoom <- as.Date(c("2001-07-01", "2001-10-31"))
views <- c(year = "Whole year", spawn = "July to October")
yv <- rbind(cbind(yr, view = "year"), cbind(yr[yr$date >= zoom[1] & yr$date <= zoom[2], ], view = "spawn"))
yv$view <- factor(yv$view, names(views))
# the ice months, shaded on the whole-year panels only
ice <- data.frame(view = factor("year", names(views)), start = as.Date(c("2001-01-01", "2001-11-01")),
                  end = as.Date(c("2001-04-30", "2001-12-31")))
top <- tapply(yv$q, list(yv$station_number, yv$view), max, na.rm = TRUE)
strip <- do.call(rbind, lapply(stations, function(st) {
  data.frame(station_number = st, view = factor(c("year", "spawn"), names(views)), window = windows$window,
             start = as.Date(paste0("2001-", windows$start)), end = as.Date(paste0("2001-", windows$end)),
             y = -top[st, c("year", "spawn")] * 0.08, h = top[st, c("year", "spawn")] * 0.05)
}))
stopifnot(identical(strip$window[strip$view == "spawn"], rep("Spawning", length(stations))))
strip$label_x <- strip$end + 4
# one colour means the last ten years here and in the change figure below
pal_period <- c(base = pal_hydro$values[["median"]], recent = pal_side$values[["below"]])
lab_period <- c(base = base_text, recent = recent_text)
cap_hydro <- sprintf(paste(
  "Daily flow at each gauge: the whole year (left), with the chinook salmon life history timing window for migration beneath, and July",
  "to October (right), with the one for spawning, on its own scale. Lines are the mean (solid) and",
  "median (dashed) day over the years of each gauge's %s normal (grey) and over %s (colour). A",
  "normal line is drawn on days with at least %d of those years on record, so at the Bulkley gauge it",
  "runs only from %s; a %s line on days each of the gauge's recent years has a record (%d at Buck",
  "Creek, which has no 2016). The shaded months, November to April, are when the gauges can read",
  "under ice."
), base_text, recent_text, min_baseline, span_003, recent_text, n_recent[["08EE013"]])
```

The same comparison day by day: the last ten years' mean and median day against `r base_text`'s,
over the whole year and, on its own scale, over the months around spawning, where the spring freshet
would otherwise flatten the low summer flow.

```{r hydrograph, fig.height = 6.5, fig.cap = cap_hydro}
ice2 <- merge(ice, data.frame(station_number = stations))
ggplot() +
  geom_rect(data = by_station(ice2), aes(xmin = start, xmax = end, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf),
            fill = pal_hydro$values[["band"]], alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_rect(data = by_station(strip), aes(xmin = start, xmax = end, ymin = y - h / 2, ymax = y + h / 2),
            fill = pal_hydro$values[["window"]]) +
  geom_text(data = by_station(strip), aes(x = label_x, y = y, label = window), hjust = 0, size = 2.4) +
  geom_line(data = by_station(yv), aes(date, q, colour = period, linetype = stat,
                                       group = interaction(period, stat)), linewidth = 0.55) +
  facet_wrap(~ station_number + view, ncol = 2, scales = "free",
             labeller = labeller(station_number = as_labeller(sub(" \\(.*", "", station_label)),
                                 view = as_labeller(views), .multi_line = FALSE)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = pal_period, labels = lab_period, name = NULL) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c(mean = "solid", median = "22"),
                        labels = c(mean = "Mean day", median = "Median day"), name = NULL) +
  # month initials on the whole-year panels, names on the July-October ones
  scale_x_date(breaks = function(l) {
    b <- seq(as.Date(cut(l[1], "month")), l[2], by = "month")
    b[b >= l[1] & b <= l[2] - 10]   # no label clipped at a panel's right edge
  }, expand = c(0.01, 0),
  labels = function(x) if (sum(!is.na(x)) > 6) substr(format(x, "%b"), 1, 1) else format(x, "%b")) +
  # no ticks among the strips below zero: they are rows, not flows
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = function(l) {
    b <- pretty(l)
    b[b >= 0]
  }) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Daily flow (m³/s)") +
  theme(panel.grid.major.x = element_blank())
```

## How much has mean flow changed?

Each point is the change in a chinook salmon life history timing window's mean flow, from its `r base_text` mean to the mean of
`r recent_text`. Its bar spans the middle 90% of changes from resampling the years in each period.
With ten recent years or fewer, that bar is narrower than a 90% confidence interval: it shows the
spread of the resamples, not a test.

```{r change, fig.height = 2.4, fig.cap = cap_change}
cd_plot <- chg
cd_plot$station_number <- factor(cd_plot$station_number, rev(stations))
cd_plot <- by_window(cd_plot)
ggplot(cd_plot, aes(pct, station_number)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = pal_hydro$values[["median"]], linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = lo, xmax = hi), height = 0, colour = pal_side$values[["below"]]) +
  geom_point(size = 2.2, colour = pal_side$values[["below"]]) +
  facet_wrap(~ period, nrow = 1) +
  scale_y_discrete(labels = function(x) sub(" \\(.*", "", station_label[x])) +
  labs(x = "Change in mean flow (%)", y = NULL)
```

## How were the numbers made?

These calls produced each chinook salmon life history timing window's mean flow, with normal and departure from the R package
[`cd`](https://newgraphenvironment.github.io/cd/) [@cd]. They read HYDAT, the
[water-temp-bc](https://github.com/NewGraphEnvironment/water-temp-bc) archive and ECCC's real-time feed
(through [`tidyhydat`](https://docs.ropensci.org/tidyhydat/) [@tidyhydat]), so the article runs on a
cached copy of their output.

```{r recipe, echo = TRUE, eval = FALSE}
library(wet)

# HYDAT, then ECCC provisional, then real-time, per station
daily <- wet_station_daily(c("08EE013", "08EE003"))

windows <- data.frame(window = c("Migration", "Spawning"), start = c("05-01", "08-01"),
                      end = c("08-01", "09-15"))
stats <- wet_window_stats(daily, windows, stats = "mean")

# normal and departure are cd's, one station per call
buck <- stats[stats$station_number == "08EE013", names(stats) != "station_number"]
base <- cd::cd_baseline(buck, 1981:2010)
departure <- cd::cd_anomaly(buck, base)
```

## What does it not show?

```{r limits}
hydat_end <- max(daily$date[daily$source == "hydat"])
n_prov <- length(unique(kf$year[kf$status == "provisional"]))
stopifnot(n_prov > 0)   # the bullet says the latest years are provisional
# "N of the ten years rest on provisional flows": every bar in those years has provisional days
prov_years <- unique(kf$year[kf$status == "provisional"])
stopifnot(all(kf$frac_provisional[kf$year %in% prov_years] > 0))
```

- **The latest years are provisional:** approved HYDAT flows end in
  `r format(hydat_end, "%B %Y")`, so `r n_prov` of the ten years `r if (n_prov == 1) "rests" else "rest"` on provisional flows, which may be
  revised.
- **Some bars have days missing:** `r nrow(part)` of the `r nrow(kf)` bars rest on
  `r pct(part_share[1])`–`r pct(part_share[2])` of their days: `r part_text`.
- **Some normals have years missing:** a year is left out of a chinook salmon life history timing window's normal when the
  window has under `r need_text` of its days, so `r miss_text`.
- **The windows come from the literature, not from observation:** New Graph's species-timing
  table cites @gottesfeld_rabnett2007SkeenaFish for both.

## Software and citation

The flows in this article are cached from HYDAT release `r prov$hydat`, with provisional and real-time
flows retrieved `r day_text(prov$retrieved)`. The chinook salmon life history timing windows are New Graph's species-timing table
at commit `r substr(prov$knowledge_sha, 1, 7)`, and the catchments, the stream mouths and the rivers
they join are the Freshwater Atlas's.

The software, each cited:

- [`wet`](https://newgraphenvironment.github.io/wet/) [@wet] reads the gauge records and makes the
  window statistics.
- [`cd`](https://newgraphenvironment.github.io/cd/) [@cd] takes the normal and the departures.
- [`tidyhydat`](https://docs.ropensci.org/tidyhydat/) [@tidyhydat] reads the ECCC real-time feed.
- [`fwapg`](https://smnorris.github.io/fwapg/) [@norris2024smnorrisfwapg] loads the Freshwater Atlas
  into PostgreSQL and delineates each gauge's catchment from it.
- [`ggplot2`](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/) [@ggplot2], [`gq`](https://newgraphenvironment.github.io/gq/)
  [@gq] and [`sf`](https://r-spatial.github.io/sf/) [@sf] make the figures and the map;
  [`knitr`](https://yihui.org/knitr/) [@knitr] and [`bookdown`](https://pkgs.rstudio.com/bookdown/)
  [@bookdown] render the article, all in R [@base].

```{r versions, results = "asis"}
# our packages' version, and the commit where the install recorded a full git hash
# (a build from a checkout records none)
ours <- vapply(c("wet", "cd", "gq"), function(p) {
  sha <- utils::packageDescription(p)$RemoteSha
  sha <- if (!is.null(sha) && grepl("^[0-9a-f]{40}$", sha)) paste0(", commit ", substr(sha, 1, 7)) else ""
  sprintf("`%s` %s%s", p, utils::packageVersion(p), sha)
}, "")
cat("This build ran on ", and_text(ours), ". To cite `wet`:\n\n", sep = "")
cat(format(utils::citation("wet"), style = "text"), sep = "\n\n")
```

### Data

- Daily flow: the Water Survey of Canada's HYDAT
  [@environmentandclimatechangecanada2021NationalWater], release `r prov$hydat`.
- Provisional and real-time daily flow: Environment and Climate Change Canada's records, as archived by
  [water-temp-bc](https://github.com/NewGraphEnvironment/water-temp-bc), and its real-time feed.
- Timing windows for chinook salmon: New Graph's species-timing table
  [@gottesfeld_rabnett2007SkeenaFish].
- Streams, lakes, catchments and place names: the Province of British Columbia's Freshwater Atlas
  [@flnrord2021FreshwaterAtlasb] and BC Geographic Names, through DataBC.

```{r wordcount, include = FALSE}
f <- knitr::current_input()
if (!is.null(f)) {
  x <- readLines(f, warn = FALSE)
  y <- utils::tail(x, -utils::head(which(x == "---"), 2)[2])   # drop the YAML header
  cite <- which(y == "## Software and citation")
  stopifnot(length(cite) == 1)
  y <- utils::head(y, cite - 1)   # the closing citation section is not body prose
  fence <- cumsum(grepl("^```", y)) %% 2 == 1
  y <- y[!fence & !grepl("^```", y)]
  y <- gsub("`r [^`]*`", "", y)          # inline code is not body prose
  y <- y[!grepl("^\\s*$", y)]
  n <- sum(lengths(strsplit(trimws(y), "\\s+")))
  message("body prose: ", n, " words")
  cap <- 750   # 600 until #145 (the answer, the window section, citations); 700 until #152 restated the window's full name per section
  if (n > cap) stop("body prose is ", n, " words; the cap is ", cap)
}
```
